source.title: Model 100A - Gray Whale
source.author: Digital Life / Johnson Martin; collaboration with Laurens Howle and Frank Fish; BOEM support
source.sourceScope: User-supplied Digital Life Model100A GLB. Embedded source UID/title/CC BY-NC4 grant agree with current public artist metadata. The artist describes a generic adult female reconstructed from images and video, not a scan or a measured named individual. Actual source GLB and two1024-square embedded PNG payloads are delivered unchanged. No online archive download or source animation was acquired.
source.delivery: Entire original supplied GLB byte-exact, including node hierarchy, original body/eye/baleen primitives, indices, UVs, colour and metallic-roughness images. Runtime applies one rigid orientation/uniform display normalization and authored same-surface jaw, posterior/fluke/pectoral and body-centred posture derivatives. No photograph projection or replacement pigment atlas.
source.biology: Artist generic adult female exterior compared qualitatively with NOAA gray-whale anatomy, the retained licensed whole profile photo and five private user comparisons: three live photographs and two illustrations. Not an independent taxonomic determination, specimen fit or optical calibration.
changes: Replaces the earlier generated exterior with the supplied sculpted gray-whale source, retaining original irregular skin/UV maps, eyes, dorsal knuckles, flippers, flukes, oral floor/roof and short baleen.
Existing lower anterior jaw membership is bound by actual source triangle adjacency; no new elliptical mouth, generic lip overlay, replacement baleen or source-surface cut.

Selected3.7-degree maximum small jaw aperture and minor anterior gular-floor change in a finite16-second benthic exterior study;107.5-degree right roll and -14-degree pitch are context from one northern Puget Sound study, not a fitted animal or universal strategy.

Finite12-second posterior stroke, selected distal fluke pitch and small pectoral stabilization; stopped glide and body-centred turn/side-roll studies. No source rig/clip, hydrodynamics, complete swimming or suction/filtration/swallowing simulation.

viewerRig.description: Same original Digital Life body/eye/baleen surfaces, UVs and two source images across finite authored external studies. Real source-adjacency jaw membership; no calibrated living kinematics or physiological controller.
viewerRig.sourceStudy: No source skeleton, morph targets or animation was supplied.

limitations: Generic artist head, eye, blowhole, flipper/fluke proportions, individual scar/epibiont identification and tissue limits remain unmeasured. Original1024-square maps are artist textures, not a photometric specimen skin. No living scan, photorealism or independent biological validation is established.

Finite exterior studies retain original geometry/UVs/maps, with selected3.7-degree aperture, minor anterior gular change, posterior/fluke/pectoral articulation and body-centred orientation. Full trajectories, speed, thrust, seabed contact, sediment/prey transport, suction pressure, hyolingual musculature, filtration, swallowing and physiology remain unfinished.

Software compatibility views only; final WebGL optics remain unreviewed. Five private supplied comparison images are not redistributed or projected onto the model. Three are live photographs, two are illustrations; their captions do not establish specimen measurements or a normal feeding sequence.
